standingQuestions.question: How large is French GDP, in total and per inhabitant, and how fast has it grown in volume each year and over the most recent quarters?
Which expenditure components (household consumption, government consumption, investment, net trade, inventories) have carried or held back GDP volume growth in each year?
How is value added distributed across branches of activity, and how has that distribution shifted, from broad sectors down to individual industries?
How is value added shared between labour, capital and net taxes, once the self-employed are credited with a wage?
How has French GDP measured in US dollars at market exchange rates evolved, and how much of each year's change comes from real growth, domestic price change and the euro-dollar exchange rate?
How do French GDP volume growth and GDP per inhabitant at purchasing power parity compare with those of other OECD economies?

How much of the level and evolution of GDP per inhabitant, in France and in other OECD economies, comes from productivity per hour worked, hours per worker, the employment rate of the working-age population and the working-age share of the population?
How unevenly is GDP per inhabitant spread across the French departements?

indicators: GDP at current prices and in chained 2020 euros, and GDP per inhabitant, annual, France, INSEE annual national accounts base 2020, 1949 onward
GDP volume growth rate, annual, 1950 onward
GDP in chained volumes, quarterly, seasonally and working-day adjusted, INSEE quarterly national accounts base 2020, used as an annualised quarterly tail after the annual series
Contributions of expenditure components to GDP volume growth, annual, 1950 onward, by component and institutional sector
Gross value added by branch at current prices and in chained volumes, A5/A10/A17/A38/A88 nomenclature levels (A10 from 1949, A38 complete from 1959, A88 complete from 1999)
Compensation of employees (D1) and gross operating surplus plus mixed income (B2G+B3G), total economy and by branch; net taxes on production and on products derived as national-accounts residuals
Domestic employment split into employees and non-employees, annual, from INSEE national accounts, for the AMECO-method adjusted wage share
GDP in current US dollars, GDP in current and constant local currency, GDP deflator and the official local-currency-per-dollar exchange rate, annual, France, World Bank WDI, 1960 onward

GDP and GDP per inhabitant in current and constant PPP US dollars, GDP volume, population, employment, average hours worked and GDP per hour worked, annual, OECD members, OECD Productivity Database, 1970 onward where published
Working-age (15-64) share of the population, annual, by country, UN World Population Prospects (existing snapshot)
GDP per inhabitant in euros and in purchasing power standards by NUTS 3 region (departement), annual, Eurostat regional accounts, 2000 onward
Departement boundary geometry keyed by INSEE departement code (existing dataset)
discovery.context: A public report on French GDP, scoped with the requester on 2026-09-22. The reader is Yann, an economics PhD: definitions of standard national-accounts concepts need no pedagogy, but data quirks do need stating (chained-volume non-additivity, the shorter A88 time span, mixed income, imputed rents of owner-occupiers inside operating surplus, commuting distortion of departement GDP per inhabitant, UN WPP projection years). Agreed decisions: (1) the headline series is annual from 1949 with a quarterly tail for the most recent years, the seam defined relative to the latest published quarter, quarterly levels annualised and quarterly growth expressed year on year; (2) demand-side decomposition uses INSEE's published contributions, which are additive, never chained component levels; (3) branch drill-down A10 -> A38 -> A88, each level on its own time span, shares shown at current prices; (4) the labour share uses the AMECO adjustment, crediting each non-employee with the average compensation per employee; (5) both GDP in current US dollars at market exchange rates, with a stacked decomposition into real growth, GDP deflator change and exchange-rate change, and GDP per inhabitant at PPP for living-standard comparison; PPP from 1970 via OECD; (6) country selector with France always shown, OECD members selectable, default comparators Germany, United Kingdom and United States; (7) the GDP-per-inhabitant decomposition is shown both for France over time and against the selected comparators; (8) departement GDP per inhabitant as a choropleth on the existing departement geometry. Output gap, household disposable income and revision/vintage analysis were proposed and declined.
discovery.readingBehavior: Read top to bottom on first visit, then revisited after each INSEE annual accounts release (end of May) and each quarterly GDP release to check the latest observation and the recent quarterly path. Exploratory within sections: drilling from broad branches into A88 industries, changing the represented period, selecting a single year across figures, and adding or removing comparator countries.

sourceDecisions.need: French annual national accounts: GDP at current prices and in chained volumes, GDP per inhabitant, expenditure contributions to growth, value added and income components by branch at A5 to A88 detail, and domestic employment split into employees and non-employees

candidates.authority: Institut national de la statistique et des etudes economiques (INSEE), producer of the French national accounts
candidates.coverage: France, 1949 to the latest provisional year (2025 when queried on 2026-09-22). Verified dataflows CNA-2020-PIB (GDP, GDP per inhabitant and contributions to growth, from 1949/1950), CNA-2020-CPEB (1,890 branch series across A5, A10, A17, A38, A88; operations P1, P2, B1G, D1, D11, D12, B2G, B2G+B3G; current prices and chained 2020 euros) and CNA-2020-EMPLOI (683 series; domestic employment by employment type E10/E20/E21/E30, hours worked, from 1949)
candidates.granularity: Annual national totals; branch detail at five nested nomenclature levels; A88 starts in 1959, 1993 or 1999 depending on the industry; A38 compensation partly from 1978
candidates.stability: Stable dataflow identifiers and IDBANKs within a base; a new base (2010, 2014, 2020) is published as new dataflows and old bases are kept, so a base change is a detectable new source rather than a silent restatement. About 400 CPEB and 200 EMPLOI series carry LAST_UPDATE 2024-06-21 and end in 2022 or 2023, i.e. have not been extended since the base-2020 launch; an assertion must surface this rather than treat it as current
candidates.accessMethod: Credential-free HTTPS GET against the INSEE BDM SDMX 2.1 endpoint https://bdm.insee.fr/series/sdmx/data/<dataflow>, the access method already proven by the insee-cpi and insee-labour-market sources
candidates.attribution: Source: INSEE, comptes nationaux annuels, base 2020
candidates.cadence: Annual. Provider evidence: every current series in CNA-2020-PIB and the maintained CPEB/EMPLOI series carry LAST_UPDATE 2026-05-29 with 2025 as latest year
candidates.publicationSchedule: Once a year at the end of May, with the provisional year N-1, semi-definitive N-2 and definitive N-3 accounts published together; observed 2026-05-29. INSEE announces the exact date in its release calendar
candidates.redistributionConstraints: Licence Ouverte 2.0 permits reuse, adaptation and redistribution including commercially, conditional only on attributing the producer and the date of the last update; no share-alike obligation

candidates.authority: Eurostat, republishing national accounts transmitted by INSEE under the ESA 2010 transmission programme
candidates.coverage: France and every EU member; main aggregates from 1975 or 1995 depending on the table; branch detail at NACE A64 from 1995
candidates.granularity: Annual; branch detail at A10/A21/A64, not INSEE's A38/A88 and not back to 1949
candidates.stability: Stable dataset codes; figures follow national transmission with a lag
candidates.licence: Eurostat reuse policy: reuse is authorised for commercial and non-commercial purposes provided the source is acknowledged (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU)
candidates.cadence: Annual, with quarterly updates of recent years
candidates.publicationSchedule: After the national release; structurally later than INSEE
candidates.redistributionConstraints: Reuse and redistribution permitted with acknowledgement of the source; no share-alike obligation

candidates.authority: OECD, republishing national accounts transmitted by INSEE
candidates.coverage: OECD members, mostly from 1970; France expenditure table longer
candidates.granularity: Annual main aggregates and ISIC broad branches; no A38/A88 industry detail
candidates.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), the OECD default licence for its statistical data
candidates.redistributionConstraints: CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution and an indication of changes; no share-alike obligation

sourceDecisions.rationale: Only INSEE carries the 1949 start, the published additive contributions to growth, the A38/A88 branch detail and the employment split needed for the adjusted wage share, all from one release. Eurostat and OECD republish the same figures later, shorter and coarser. The three dataflows share one release and one provider, so they form one source package.
